'''''God of War'''''{{efn|Colloquially referred to as ''God of War 4'', ''God of War IV'',<ref name="GodofWar4"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/gaming/feature/a813161/god-of-war-4-ps4-trailer-release-date-price-gameplay/|title=God of War 4 PS4 trailers, release date, price, gameplay and everything we know so far|date=March 24, 2017|last1=Loveridge|first1=Sam|last2=Mahboubian-Jones|first2=Justin|publisher=[[Hearst Magazines UK]]|work=[[Digital Spy]]|access-date=June 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413185255/https://www.digitalspy.com/gaming/feature/a813161/god-of-war-4-ps4-trailer-release-date-price-gameplay/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/new-god-of-war-trailer-e3-2017/|title=In The New 'God of War 4' Trailer, Kratos Is Old, Grizzled, And As Brutal As Ever|date=June 13, 2017|last=Wagner|first=Jayce|publisher=Designtechnica Corp.|work=[[Digital Trends]]|access-date=June 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413185407/https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/new-god-of-war-trailer-e3-2017/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> ''God of War PS4'',<ref name="single-player-only"/><ref name="nomultiplayer"/> and ''God of War 2018''<ref name="annoying"/>}} is a 2018 [[action-adventure game]] developed by [[Santa Monica Studio]] and published by [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]. It was released worldwide for the [[PlayStation 4]] in April 2018, with a [[Windows]] port released in January 2022. It is the eighth game in the [[God of War (franchise)|''God of War'' series]] and the sequel to 2010's ''[[God of War III]]''.

While previous games were based on [[Greek mythology]], ''God of War'' transitioned to [[Norse mythology]], and takes places in mythical ancient [[Scandinavia]] in the realm of [[Midgard]]. Players control [[Kratos (God of War)|Kratos]], who embarks on a journey with his son, [[Atreus (God of War)|Atreus]], to scatter the ashes of Atreus's mother from the highest peak of the [[Norse cosmology|nine realms]]. Kratos keeps his past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware he is a [[demigod]]. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and [[List of Germanic deities|gods of the Norse world]].

Described by creative director [[Cory Barlog]] as a reimagining of the franchise, a major [[gameplay]] change is that Kratos now uses a magical [[battle axe]], the Leviathan Axe, instead of his signature [[Dual wield|double-chained blades]]. The game also uses an [[Virtual camera system#Interactive|over-the-shoulder free camera]], with the game in [[One-shot film|one shot]], as opposed to the [[Virtual camera system#Fixed|fixed cinematic camera]] of the previous entries. It also includes [[role-playing video game|role-playing game]] elements, and Kratos's son Atreus provides assistance in combat. The majority of the original game's development team worked on ''God of War'' and designed it to be accessible and grounded. A short [[text-based game]], ''[[A Call from the Wilds]]'', was released in February 2018 through [[Facebook Messenger]] and follows Atreus on his first adventure. A smartphone app, ''Mímir's Vision'', was released three days before the release, providing additional information about the Norse setting.

''God of War'' received acclaim for its story, world design, art direction, music, graphics, combat system, and characters, in particular the dynamic between Kratos and Atreus. Many reviewers felt it had successfully revitalized the series without losing its core identity. It was named [[List of Game of the Year awards|Game of the Year]] by numerous media outlets and award shows, and has been cited as among the [[greatest video games ever made|greatest video games]]. It sold more than five million copies within a month of release and had sold 23 million by November 2022, making it one of the [[best-selling PlayStation 4 games]] and the best-selling game in the series. A [[novelization]] was released in August 2018, followed by [[God of War (Dark Horse Comics)|a prequel comic series]] published from November 2018 to June 2021, while a [[live-action]] television series is in development for [[Amazon Prime Video]]. A sequel, ''[[God of War Ragnarök]]'', was released for the PlayStation 4 and [[PlayStation 5]] in 2022, and for Windows in 2024.

==Gameplay==
''God of War'' is an [[action-adventure game]]. Unlike the previous games, which mostly use a [[Virtual camera system#Fixed|fixed cinematic camera]], it uses an [[Virtual camera system#Interactive|over-the-shoulder camera]].<ref name="GS-E32016" /> It is presented in a [[One shot (film)|continuous shot]], with no [[camera cut]]s or [[loading screen]]s.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bratt|first1=Chris|title=God of War director explains why entire game has no camera cuts|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-06-21-god-of-war-director-explains-why-the-entire-game-has-no-camera-cuts|access-date=April 13, 2018|work=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|date=June 21, 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194731/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2017-06-21-god-of-war-director-explains-why-the-entire-game-has-no-camera-cuts|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Although the previous main installment, ''[[God of War: Ascension|Ascension]]'' (2013), introduced [[multiplayer]] to the series, this installment is [[single-player]]-only.<ref name="single-player-only">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-doesnt-include-multiplayer-wont-be-/1100-6441104/|title=God of War PS4 Doesn't Include Multiplayer, Won't Be Kratos's Last Game|date=June 21, 2016|last=Paget|first=Mat|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413193804/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-doesnt-include-multiplayer-wont-be-/1100-6441104/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Regarding the level structure, creative director [[Cory Barlog]] said "it's open, but it is not an [[open world]]."<ref name="newgameplay"/> Due to its openness, a [[fast travel]] feature is unlocked later.<ref name="GIquestions">{{cite AV media |people=[[Cory Barlog|Barlog, Cory]]; Hanson, Ben|date=February 2, 2018|title=Answering God Of War's Lingering Questions|medium=[[YouTube]]|language=en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ViaCWvqwUwU|access-date=February 4, 2018|publisher=[[Game Informer]], [[GameStop]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413190025/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ViaCWvqwUwU|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Swimming, an ability in previous games, was cut;<ref name="GIp38"/> players instead use a boat to traverse bodies of water.<ref name="GIquestions"/> Unlike previous games, which allowed players to jump freely at any time, jumping can now only be done at designated areas, such as at a rock face or ledge. Players battle [[Norse mythology|Norse mythological]] foes, like [[Dökkálfar and Ljósálfar|dark elves]], [[wulver]]s, and [[draugr]]s,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/videos/god-of-war-the-lost-pages-of-norse-myth-rise-of-th/2300-6441090/|title=God Of War – The Lost Pages Of Norse Myth: Rise Of The Draugr|date=September 27, 2017|last=Kulasingham|first=Gajan|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=February 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194834/https://www.gamespot.com/videos/god-of-war-the-lost-pages-of-norse-myth-rise-of-th/2300-6441090/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> as well as [[Gullveig]] and the [[revenant]]s, beings warped by [[seiðr]] magic, among many others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/videos/god-of-war-the-lost-pages-of-norse-myth-manifestat/2300-6441135/|title=God Of War – The Lost Pages Of Norse Myth: Manifestation Of The Revenant|date=September 29, 2017|last=Kulasingham|first=Gajan|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=February 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194940/https://www.gamespot.com/videos/god-of-war-the-lost-pages-of-norse-myth-manifestat/2300-6441135/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> [[Valkyrie]]s appear as optional secret [[boss battles]] throughout the six playable locations.<ref name="ign valkyrie">{{Cite web |title=God of War Valkyrie Locations and Hidden Chambers - God of War (2018) Wiki Guide |url=https://www.ign.com/wikis/god-of-war-2018/God_of_War_Valkyrie_Locations_and_Hidden_Chambers |access-date=May 5, 2023|website=IGN |date=April 25, 2018 |language=en |archive-date=May 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505010604/https://www.ign.com/wikis/god-of-war-2018/God_of_War_Valkyrie_Locations_and_Hidden_Chambers |url-status=live }}</ref> Among the many [[side quest]]s, players can free the imprisoned [[dragon]]s [[Fáfnir]], [[Ótr|Otr]], and [[Regin]]n—[[Dwarf (folklore)|dwarves]] who were turned into dragons—in addition to battling one called Hræzlyr, a story-based boss battle.<ref name="GIquestions"/><ref name="exploration"/>

The in-game [[Head-up display (video gaming)|HUD]] can be seen in the bottom left and right corners. The left shows information for Kratos, such as his [[Health (gaming)|health]] and what [[runic]] attacks are equipped. The right shows similar information for [[Atreus (God of War)|Atreus]].|alt=A GIF that shows the character Kratos throwing his weapon, the Leviathan Axe, at an enemy, magically freezing it in place. Important character information is shown in both bottom corners.]]
The player controls the character [[Kratos (God of War)|Kratos]] in [[Combo (video gaming)|combo-based combat]] and [[Puzzle video game|puzzle game]] elements. The [[gameplay]] was completely rebuilt from previous games.<ref name="newgameplay">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-set-after-third-game-wont-be-open-w/1100-6440887/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0a|title=New God of War Set After Third Game, Won't Be Open World|date=June 14, 2016|last=Paget|first=Mat|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=June 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194345/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-set-after-third-game-wont-be-open-w/1100-6440887/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0a|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> A major change is that Kratos no longer uses his signature [[Dual wield|double-chained blades]], the Blades of Chaos, as his default weapon. Instead, he uses a magical [[battle axe]] called the Leviathan Axe,<ref name="axeorigin">{{cite web|url=https://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2017/12/13/god-of-war-podcast-details-the-origin-of-the-leviathan-axe/|title=Latest God of War Podcast Episode Details the Origin of the Leviathan Axe|date=December 13, 2017|last=Henges|first=Elizabeth|publisher=[[CraveOnline]]|work=[[PlayStation LifeStyle]]|access-date=December 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413195038/https://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2017/12/13/god-of-war-podcast-details-the-origin-of-the-leviathan-axe/|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> which is infused with ice elemental [[Magic (gaming)|magic]]. The axe can be thrown at enemies and magically summoned back to his hand, similar to [[Thor]]'s hammer [[Mjölnir]]. Larger enemies have precision targets which stun the enemy if hit. The weapon can also be thrown at objects to freeze or move mechanisms, or trigger damaging explosions, until returned to Kratos's hand. The axe has standard light and heavy attacks. Over time, it can be upgraded with [[runes]] to allow for light and heavy magical "runic" attacks. This provides players with a variety of options to cater to their own play style.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|pp=40–41}}</ref> Another new weapon is the collapsible Guardian Shield, which appears as a [[vambrace]] on his arm when not in use. The shield can be used offensively or defensively, similar to the [[Golden Fleece]] in previous games.<ref name="E32017"/> Kratos also utilizes hand-to-hand combat, a feature originally introduced in ''Ascension''.<ref name="GS-E32016"/> The Blades of Chaos, infused with fire elemental magic, are acquired later via a plot device and perform in a similar manner as in previous installments—they are a pair of blades [[Chain weapon|attached to chains]] that can be swung around in various maneuvers. The weapon can also be upgraded with magical runic attacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/god-of-war-4-blades-of-chaos/|title=How Kratos Gets The Blades of Chaos Back in God of War 4|date=April 21, 2018|last=Little|first=Riley|work=[[Screen Rant]]|publisher=Valnet, Inc.|access-date=November 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119091900/https://screenrant.com/god-of-war-4-blades-of-chaos/|archive-date=November 19, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

As in the earlier games, there is a "Rage" ability, this one called Spartan Rage. Like in previous games, the Rage ability has a meter that gradually fills during combat. With this ability, Kratos uses powerful bare-handed attacks, as opposed to weapons, to greatly damage enemies. The game also features [[role-playing video game|role-playing game]] (RPG) elements.<ref name="GS-E32016"/><ref name="GIp41">{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|p=41}}</ref> There are crafting resources for the player to find that allow them to create new or upgrade existing armor with better [[Experience point#Perks|perks]].<ref name="MadeMeCare"/> Players also accumulate a currency called Hacksilver, a key component in crafting and purchasing new [[Item (gaming)|items]]. [[Experience point]]s (XP) are used for learning new combat skills.<ref name="GIp41"/> Players find chests containing random items, such as enchantments for improving armor and weapons, as well as the Hacksilver currency. There are also two special items, [[Iðunn]]'s [[Golden apple|Apples]] and [[Drinking horn|horns]] of Blood Mead, which increase Kratos's maximum [[Health (gaming)|health]] and Rage, respectively. These meters are replenished by [[Power-up#Health and life reserves|green]] and [[Power-up#Ammunition and power reserves|red orbs]] dropped by downed foes and found throughout the game world. For the magical runic attacks, instead of collecting blue orbs to replenish the ability (like in the previous games), there is a [[Glossary of video game terms#cooldown|cooldown]] timer for each ability.<ref name="p42-43">{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|pp=42–43}}</ref>

[[Quick time event]]s have changed from previous games.<ref name="newgameplay"/> Enemies display two meters above their heads, one for health (the color of which indicates the enemy's difficulty) and the other for stun. Filling the stun meter helps to defeat more difficult enemies. When the stun meter is full, a grab prompt will appear. Depending on the enemy, Kratos may rip them in half or grab them and throw them into other enemies, among other possible outcomes.<ref name="GIp42">{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|p=42}}</ref> Although the game is played entirely as Kratos,<ref name="SegmentNext"/> there are times when the player may choose to passively control his son, [[Atreus (God of War)|Atreus]]. One button is dedicated to Atreus, and its use depends on the context. For example, if the player needs assistance, they can look at an enemy and press the button, and Atreus will shoot an arrow at the enemy.<ref name="TakeKratosSeriously">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-director-on-the-challenge-of-making/1100-6440945/|title=God of War PS4 Director on the Challenge of Making People Take Kratos Seriously|date=June 15, 2016|last=Hussain|first=Tamoor|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=June 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413193941/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-director-on-the-challenge-of-making/1100-6440945/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Over the course of the game, Atreus helps in combat, traversal, exploration, and puzzle-solving. When facing a large number of enemies, he distracts the weaker ones as Kratos fights the stronger ones.<ref name="MadeMeCare">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2016/06/14/e3-2016-god-of-war-made-me-care-about-the-series-for-the-first-time|title=E3 2016: God of War Made Me Care About The Series For The First Time|date=June 14, 2016|last=Sliva|first=Marty|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|work=[[IGN]]|access-date=June 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413195831/https://www.ign.com/articles/2016/06/14/e3-2016-god-of-war-made-me-care-about-the-series-for-the-first-time|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> If too many enemies gang up on Atreus, he is briefly stunned, but he cannot be knocked out or killed. Atreus also acquires new skills, armor, and runic attacks, as well as special light and shock arrows for his bow. Atreus's runic attacks summon different spectral animals with different abilities. For example, one summons a pack of wolves that attacks enemies, while another summons the squirrel [[Ratatoskr]], who will dig up health and rage orbs.<ref name="p42-43"/>

==Synopsis==
===Setting===
While the [[God of War (franchise)#First era (Greek mythology)|first seven games]] were loosely based on [[Greek mythology]], this installment is loosely inspired by Norse mythology, taking place at least 150 years after ''[[God of War III]]'' (2010).<ref name="WCCF"/> Six of the [[Norse cosmology|nine realms of Norse mythology]] can be explored. Predating the [[Vikings]],<ref name="TakeKratosSeriously"/><ref name="Egypt"/> most of the game takes place in ancient [[Scandinavia]] in the realm of [[Midgard]], which is inhabited by humans and other creatures. It is the same realm in which the Greek world existed. As more dangerous creatures began appearing, many humans fled. Other realms visited as part of the story include [[Alfheim]], the mystical home of the [[Dökkálfar and Ljósálfar|light and dark elves]]; [[Helheim]], the icy land of the dead; and [[Jötunheim]], the mountainous land of the [[Jötunn|Giants]]. Optional explorable realms include [[Niflheim]], a realm of poisonous fog with a maze-like structure of rewards; and the fire realm [[Muspelheim]], featuring the six Trials of Muspelheim—completing each trial grants rewards and advances Kratos and Atreus closer to the top of a large volcano, facing off [[Göndul]], one of the nine [[Valkyrie]]s.<ref name="ign valkyrie"/> Access to the other three realms—[[Asgard]], home of the [[Æsir]] gods; [[Vanaheim]], home of the [[Vanir]] gods; and [[Svartalfheim]], home of the dwarves—has been blocked by [[Odin]], the ruler of Asgard and the Æsir gods.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamerevolution.com/guides/383529-god-of-war-unlock-realms|title=God of War How to Unlock Realms|date=April 19, 2018|last=Faulkner|first=Jason|work=[[Game Revolution]]|publisher=[[CraveOnline]]|access-date=April 25, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180426171355/https://www.gamerevolution.com/guides/383529-god-of-war-unlock-realms|archive-date=April 26, 2018}}</ref> At the center of the realms is the [[Trees in mythology|mythical tree]] [[Yggdrasil]], which connects each realm. Although each realm is a different world, they exist simultaneously in the same space. Travel to and from realms can be done by using the [[Bifröst]] from a root of Yggdrasil contained within Týr's Temple at the center of the Lake of the Nine. The temple was created by its namesake, [[Týr]], a peaceful God of War who traveled to other lands and learned about their mythologies; it was told that Odin had him killed as he believed Týr was secretly aiding the Giants and would try to overthrow him.<ref name="WCCF"/>

===Characters===
{{main|Characters of God of War}}
Kratos ([[Christopher Judge]]) is a warrior from [[Sparta]] who became the Greek God of War and is a son of [[Zeus]]. After ending up in ancient Scandinavia following his [[God of War (franchise)#First era (Greek mythology)|war against Olympus]], he met his second wife, [[Laufey (mythology)|Laufey]] (addressed as Faye), who died from an unknown cause. Their son, Atreus ([[Sunny Suljic]])., does not know about Kratos's past or his divine nature but can hear other beings' thoughts. The main antagonist is the Æsir god [[Baldur]] ([[Jeremy Davies]]), the half-brother of [[Thor]], whose sons [[Modi and Magni]] ([[Nolan North]] and [[Troy Baker]], respectively) assist him. Baldur's parents are Odin, the Allfather and King of the Æsir, and the Vanir goddess [[Freya]] ([[Danielle Bisutti]]), the former Queen of the Valkyries. Freya tried leaving Odin after he began corrupting her Vanir magic, but he in turn stripped her of her Valkyrie wings, banished her to Midgard, and cast a spell on her that prevented her from causing harm to others and from leaving the realm. She then hid her identity under an alias, the Witch of the Woods. To protect her son from a prophecy that foretold his death, Freya cast a spell of immortality on Baldur, which also prevented him from feeling pain or pleasure. The effects of the spell caused Baldur to greatly resent his mother. The only thing capable of harming him was [[mistletoe]], a fact which Freya kept secret.<ref name="btva">{{cite web|url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/video-games/God-of-War-2018/|title=God of War (2018)|work=Behind The Voice Actors|publisher=Inyxception Enterprises|access-date=November 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112043517/https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/video-games/God-of-War-2018/|archive-date=January 12, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Other characters include [[Mímir]] ([[Alastair Duncan (Scottish actor)|Alastair Duncan]]), who claims to be the smartest man alive, and the Huldra Brothers—[[Brokkr|Brok]] (Robert Craighead) and [[Sindri (mythology)|Sindri]] ([[Adam J. Harrington]])—dwarves who appear at various points in the world and assist Kratos and Atreus by forging new gear. Weapons forged by the Huldra Brothers, including Thor's hammer Mjölnir, were used by the Æsir gods. They also forged Kratos's Leviathan Axe, which originally belonged to Faye, who also gifted Kratos her Guardian Shield.<ref name="axeorigin"/> The spirit of the Greek goddess [[Athena]] ([[Carole Ruggier]]){{efn|Carole Ruggier had previously voiced Athena in the original ''[[God of War (2005 video game)|God of War]]'' (2005) and ''[[God of War II]]'' (2007), but was replaced by Erin Torpey in subsequent games.}} makes a cameo appearance, and Zeus ([[Corey Burton]]){{efn|Corey Burton reprised the role, having previously voiced Zeus in ''[[God of War II]]'' (2007), ''[[God of War III]]'' (2010), and ''[[God of War: Ascension]]'' (2013).}} appears to Kratos as an illusion in Helheim.<ref name="btva"/>

===Plot===
Many years after defeating the [[Olympian gods]],{{efn|As depicted in ''[[God of War III]]'' (2010)}} Kratos has been living with his wife Faye and their son Atreus in Midgard. Soon after Faye dies, Kratos cremates her body, and is confronted by a stranger with godly powers. The two battle and Kratos seemingly kills the stranger, after which Kratos and Atreus begin their journey to honor Faye's last wish: to scatter her ashes at the highest peak in the nine realms. They encounter the Dwarves Brok and Sindri, the kindly Witch of the Woods, who recognizes Kratos's godhood, and [[Jörmungandr]], the World Serpent. When their path is blocked by impenetrable black mist, the Witch instructs them to travel to Alfheim and secure its magical light to extinguish the mist. Successful, they reach Midgard's peak and overhear a conversation between the stranger—revealed to be Baldur—and his nephews, Modi and Magni, as well as the imprisoned Mímir. Mímir reveals the highest peak is actually in Jötunheim, but the Giants have blocked travel there.

Knowing of another passage, Mímir instructs Kratos to behead him and have his head revived by the Witch of the Woods, whom, upon resurrection, he reveals to be the goddess Freya. Kratos's longstanding hatred of gods causes him to distrust her, but both Freya and Mímir warn him he must tell Atreus about his true nature. Kratos, Atreus, and Mímir are attacked by Modi and Magni. After Kratos kills Magni, Modi flees but later ambushes the trio. Kratos fends him off, but Atreus collapses, overcome by illness due to the contradiction of a god believing himself to be mortal. Freya instructs Kratos to retrieve the heart of a troll in Helheim; however, his frost-based Leviathan Axe is useless in the icy realm. Kratos returns home to unearth his old weapons, the fiery Blades of Chaos, and is haunted by Athena's spirit. After retrieving the heart, he has a haunting vision of Zeus. Freya revives Atreus, and Kratos tells him they are gods. Atreus becomes increasingly arrogant and, against Kratos's orders, murders a weakened Modi, who was beaten by Thor for not avenging Magni. At Midgard's peak, Baldur ambushes Kratos and Atreus, resulting in Jötunheim's portal being destroyed. Their battle descends to Týr's Temple, and the group ends up in Helheim.

Atreus makes amends with Kratos after being reprimanded. They learn of Freya and Baldur's familial relationship and the spell of invulnerability she cast on him. Returning to Midgard, Mímir realizes another way to reach Jötunheim, but needs his missing eye. After obtaining it, the group are attacked by Baldur once more, but Freya intervenes to protect her son. Baldur is pierced by Atreus's mistletoe arrow, breaking Freya's spell. Though defeated, Kratos spares him on the condition he leave both them and Freya alone; Baldur attempts to strangle Freya, causing Kratos to kill him. A grief-stricken Freya vows revenge on Kratos, and leaves with Baldur's corpse, but not before taunting him about the past he has not yet told his son. Kratos tells Atreus about his own past and how he killed many people including his own father. Atreus laments this cycle of violence, and Kratos tells him they should not repeat the mistakes of their predecessors, including those made by Kratos himself.

Kratos and Atreus reach Jötunheim. They find an abandoned temple with a mural depicting their adventures, showing that the Giants, renowned for their gift of prophecy, had foretold their journey. They discover Faye was a Giant who had decided to stay in Midgard, making Atreus half Giant, one-quarter god, and one-quarter mortal. Their fight with Baldur is shown, revealing he sought Faye the whole time under Odin's orders, unaware she was dead and Atreus was referred to as [[Loki]] by his mother and the Giants. Kratos chooses to ignore a covered mural depicting what appears to be him dying in Atreus's arms. They fulfill their promise and spread Faye's ashes at the peak. Afterward, Kratos reveals to Atreus that his given name was that of a compassionate Spartan comrade.{{efn|This Atreus appears in ''[[God of War Sons of Sparta]]'' (2026).}} Returning to Midgard, they retrieve Mímir, who warns them Baldur's death has caused the three-year-long [[Fimbulwinter]] to begin nearly a century earlier than prophesized, meaning [[Ragnarök]] is soon to follow. At home, the pair sleep, and Atreus has a vision of Thor arriving at the end of Fimbulwinter to confront them. 

==Development==
[[File:God of war 2018 santa monica team gdc 2019.jpg|thumb|right|alt= Photograph of the ''God of War'' developers at the 2019 Game Developers Choice Awards | The [[Santa Monica Studio]] team behind ''God of War'' at the 2019 [[Game Developers Choice Awards]]]]
Development on the next ''[[God of War (franchise)|God of War]]'' began in 2014. This was confirmed by [[Santa Monica Studio]]'s creative director [[Cory Barlog]] at the inaugural [[PlayStation Experience]] on December 6 that year, where Barlog said it was in early development and that it would not be a [[prequel]] but possibly a [[Reboot (fiction)|reboot]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-in-development-at-sony-santa-monica/1100-6424051/ |title=New God of War in Development at Sony Santa Monica |date=December 6, 2014 |last=Maiberg |first=Emanuel |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=[[GameSpot]] |access-date=December 7, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323072539/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-in-development-at-sony-santa-monica/1100-6424051/ |archive-date=March 23, 2015 |url-status=live  }}</ref> In April 2016, [[concept art]] was leaked that showed images of Kratos in the world of Norse mythology, a concept originally considered by series creator [[David Jaffe]] after Kratos eliminated the Greek gods.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2016/4/5/11366326/god-of-war-4-concept-art-kratos-norse-mythology |title=Rumored God of War concept art shows Kratos tackling Norse mythology |date=April 5, 2016 |last1=McWhertor |first1=Michael |last2=Good |first2=Owen |publisher=[[Vox Media]] |work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |access-date=April 5, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419115429/https://www.polygon.com/2016/4/5/11366326/god-of-war-4-concept-art-kratos-norse-mythology |archive-date=April 19, 2016 |url-status=live  }}</ref> The official announcement came at [[E3 2016]], with a gameplay demo that confirmed the setting. The demo showed a fully bearded Kratos teaching his son how to hunt. The pair also battled a [[troll]]. The end of the demo showed the title ''God of War'' and confirmed it was in development for the [[PlayStation 4]] (PS4).<ref name="GodofWar4">{{cite web |url=https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/god-war-4-kicks-off-sony-e3-2016-press-conference-1565263 |title=God of War 4 kicks off Sony E3 2016 press conference |date=June 13, 2016 |last=Skipper |first=Ben |work=[[International Business Times]] |access-date=June 13, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194600/https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/god-war-4-kicks-off-sony-e3-2016-press-conference-1565263 |archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref><ref name="GS-E32016">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-revealed-for-ps4-at-e3-2016/1100-6440819/|title=God of War Revealed for PS4 at E3 2016|date=June 13, 2016|last1=Newhouse|first1=Alex|last2=Crossley|first2=Rob|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=June 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194458/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-revealed-for-ps4-at-e3-2016/1100-6440819/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> The E3 announcement also confirmed that Barlog had returned to the series as game director for the new installment. Since the original ''[[God of War (2005 video game)|God of War]]'' (2005), Barlog had been a major contributor in the development of the series, previously most notably as the director of ''[[God of War II]]'' (2007); this installment was his fifth ''God of War'' game.<ref name="TakeKratosSeriously"/>

Barlog said the title ''God of War'' with no numeral or subtitle was chosen because, although it was a continuation of the series, "we ... [reimagined] everything".<ref name="WCCF"/><ref name="SegmentNext"/> Head of Santa Monica Studio, Shannon Studstill, and Barlog said that [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]] had to be convinced to do another ''God of War'' game as many people at Sony wanted the series to "sleep and rest" due to the lackluster response to the previous game, ''Ascension''.<ref name="GIp45">{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|p=45}}</ref> In explaining why Barlog was brought back, Studstill said he knew the series very well, "and bringing in someone that understands that history is the respect the franchise deserves".<ref name="GIp38">{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|p=38}}</ref> Barlog responded, "You gotta know the rules to break the rules."<ref name="GIp38"/> Series creator David Jaffe was also considered but was unavailable.<ref>{{cite AV media|people=Hanson, Ben; Juba, Joe|date=January 5, 2018|title=Exclusive God Of War Studio Visit Impressions|medium=[[YouTube]]|language=en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxXBNjq_BBM|access-date=February 1, 2018|publisher=[[Game Informer]], [[GameStop]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112043516/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxXBNjq_BBM|archive-date=January 12, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In explaining the transition from Greek mythology to Norse mythology, Barlog said: "It's kind of this [[Anno Domini|BC–AD]] change over kind of thing. We're moving and starting from zero and kind of moving forward on that".<ref name="WCCF"/><ref name="SegmentNext">{{cite web|url=https://segmentnext.com/2016/06/14/first-details-on-god-of-war-ps4-game-same-storyline-but-new-gameplay/|title=First Details on God of War PS4 Game; Same Storyline But New Gameplay|date=June 13, 2016|last=Lillah|first=Sarmad|publisher=SegmentNext.com|access-date=June 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413200101/https://segmentnext.com/2016/06/14/first-details-on-god-of-war-ps4-game-same-storyline-but-new-gameplay/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> In adapting the Norse myths, Barlog said there were many different translations and interpretations, and the writing team read the ''[[Prose Edda]]'' to learn how the myths were translated and told. Just like they did with Greek mythology in the previous games, they found ways to parallel path things from the Norse myths to fit their story.<ref>{{cite AV media|people=[[Cory Barlog|Barlog, Cory]]|date=March 5, 2018|title=God of War - Behind the Myths: An Interview with Cory Barlog <nowiki>|</nowiki> PS4|medium=[[YouTube]]|language=en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wxyEcgv34Rk|access-date=November 5, 2022|publisher=[[PlayStation]], [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|archive-date=November 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221105051432/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wxyEcgv34Rk|url-status=live}}</ref> Before settling on Norse mythology, [[Egyptian mythology]] was also considered. Barlog said that half of the team was for it, but because Egypt has "a lot more about civilization – it's less isolated, less barren", he decided on the Norse setting to keep the focus on Kratos. Barlog explained further: "Having too much around distracts from that central theme of a stranger in a strange land".<ref name="Egypt">{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-06-15-god-of-war-team-considered-setting-the-new-game-in-egypt|title=God of War team considered setting the new game in Egypt|date=June 15, 2016|last=Bratt|first=Chris|work=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|access-date=June 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413200511/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-06-15-god-of-war-team-considered-setting-the-new-game-in-egypt|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> To explain why Kratos was now in the Norse world, Barlog said that different cultures' belief systems coexisted, but they were "separated by geography", suggesting that Kratos traveled from Greece to Norway (Scandinavia) after the conclusion of ''God of War III''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-why-kratos-is-in-norse-mythology-no/1100-6441051/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0a&linkId=25746674|title=New God of War: Why Kratos Is in Norse Mythology Now|date=June 20, 2016|last=Paget|first=Mat|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413200657/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-why-kratos-is-in-norse-mythology-no/1100-6441051/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0a&linkId=25746674|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Clarifying the conclusion of that game, Barlog said that Kratos did not destroy what was believed to be the entire world, but only the portion ruled over by the Greek pantheon.<ref name="GIquestions"/> Barlog also said the newer game predated the Vikings, taking place in the time when their gods walked the Earth.<ref name="TakeKratosSeriously"/><ref name="Egypt"/>

Most of the development team that worked on the original ''God of War'' worked on the new installment.<ref name="WCCF"/> They said they matched the new gameplay with the same accessibility as the previous installments.<ref name="newgameplay"/> It was confirmed that the game would not feature any morality system or branching story; all players have the same story experience. The developers also confirmed that some of the more controversial minigames found in previous entries (such as one featuring sex) would not return.<ref name="WCCF"/> The enemy count was increased to up to 100 enemies on-screen, although this limit is never approached; ''God of War III'' and ''Ascension'' had up to 50.<ref name="WCCF">{{cite web|url=https://wccftech.com/god-wars-original-team-working-new-game-no-branching-story-confirmed/|title=God Of War Original Team Is Working On New Game, 100 Enemies On Screen Confirmed And More|date=June 24, 2016|last=De Meo|first=Francesco|publisher=WCCF Tech|access-date=July 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413200254/https://wccftech.com/god-wars-original-team-working-new-game-no-branching-story-confirmed/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Some gameplay characteristics such as jumping, swimming, and instant-death [[platform game|platforming challenges]] found in the previous installments were cut because of the camera being closer to Kratos.<ref name="GIp38"/> Although the previous installment, ''Ascension'', introduced multiplayer to the series, the team decided to forgo it and focus on the single-player experience.<ref name="nomultiplayer">{{cite web|url=https://attackofthefanboy.com/news/e3-2016-god-war-ps4-wont-multiplayer-mode/|title=E3 2016: God of War PS4 Won't Have A Multiplayer Mode|date=June 18, 2016|last=Seeto|first=Damian|work=Attack of the Fanboy|publisher=Modern Media Group|access-date=February 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194058/https://attackofthefanboy.com/news/e3-2016-god-war-ps4-wont-multiplayer-mode/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> In changing the gameplay, Studstill said, "I felt like, in order to reinvent, we really needed to turn a lot of things around".<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|p=36}}</ref> With regard to the camera change, Barlog said they wanted a more intimate and player-controlled experience.<ref name="newgameplay"/>

The entire game is played in a single shot with no camera cuts; there are no loading screens and no [[Fade (lighting)|fades to black]] between gameplay and cutscenes.<ref name="MadeMeCare"/> Barlog said about forty percent of the team did not originally agree with this decision due to the increased work and production to implement the feature,<ref name="Polygon Camera"/> especially since this was the first time that a one-shot technique was being used for a [[Video game graphics#3D|three-dimensional]] [[AAA game]]. This meant Barlog had no examples to show if this would work or was a good idea.{{efn|Games like ''[[Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain]]'' (2015) and ''[[Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice]]'' (2017), both in development around the same time as ''God of War'', utilized similar one-shot techniques.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hardcoregamer.com/news/god-of-war-director-cory-barlog-praises-hideo-kojima-mgs-influence/298727/|title=God of War Director Cory Barlog Praises Hideo Kojima, MGS Influence|date=May 10, 2018|last=Riaz|first=Adnan|work=Hardcore Gamer|access-date=February 10, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210071535/https://hardcoregamer.com/news/god-of-war-director-cory-barlog-praises-hideo-kojima-mgs-influence/298727/|archive-date=February 10, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>}} After the team played through the finished game, Barlog said they finally understood his vision and said it was a feature they should use from now on.<ref name="Polygon Camera">{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/4/23/17263016/god-of-war-playstation-4-camera-single-shot|title=God of War's camera was a huge risk that paid off|date=April 23, 2018|last=Kuchera|first=Ben|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|publisher=[[Vox Media]]|access-date=December 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181227133056/https://www.polygon.com/2018/4/23/17263016/god-of-war-playstation-4-camera-single-shot|archive-date=December 27, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Barlog had originally [[Pitch (filmmaking)|pitched]] the idea for a one-shot camera while he was at [[Crystal Dynamics]] working on ''[[Tomb Raider (2013 video game)|Tomb Raider]]'' (2013), but he was turned down. Sony, however, was much more supportive of Barlog's creative ideas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usgamer.net/articles/god-of-war-director-originally-pitched-one-shot-camera-idea-for-tomb-raider|title=God of War Director Originally Pitched One-Shot Camera Idea for Tomb Raider|date=March 22, 2018|last=Oxford|first=Nadia|work=[[USgamer]]|access-date=December 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181227133107/https://www.usgamer.net/articles/god-of-war-director-originally-pitched-one-shot-camera-idea-for-tomb-raider|archive-date=December 27, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Furthermore, Barlog and lead level designer Rob Davis were also influenced by the ''[[Resident Evil]]'' series, particularly ''[[Resident Evil 4]]'' (2005){{'}}s "combination of poised camera exploration and scavenging" and ''[[Resident Evil 7]]'' (2017){{'}}s "strong vision" from a team making "bold decisions, and actually hav[ing] the audience follow them". Barlog noted how there was initial disagreement over the camera distance. He wanted it close whereas the combat team wanted it further away, like the ''[[Assassin's Creed]]'' and ''[[Batman: Arkham]]'' games; he eventually convinced the team to go with a close camera.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Makuch |first1=Eddie |title=God of War PS4 Director Explains Why They Changed The Combat And More |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-director-explains-why-they-changed-/1100-6458259/ |access-date=May 30, 2019 |work=[[GameSpot]] |date=April 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530211324/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-director-explains-why-they-changed-/1100-6458259/ |archive-date=May 30, 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Explaining Kratos's axe, lead gameplay designer Jason McDonald, who had worked on the series since the original game, said the axe was chosen because they wanted a more grounded direction. Initially, they were unsure how to make it unique. After they came up with the concept of throwing the axe and having it return to Kratos, "things started to fall into place".<ref name="developingaxe">{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/15/16894114/god-of-war-kratos-ax-combat|title=Here's how God of War is different with Kratos ax|date=January 15, 2018|last=Sarkar|first=Samit|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|publisher=[[Vox Media]]|access-date=February 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413200913/https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/15/16894114/god-of-war-kratos-ax-combat|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> McDonald said that combat with the axe was a little slower than with the Blades of Chaos, "but it's just as fluid and just as brutal as it's ever been".<ref name="developingaxe"/> Barlog took inspiration from ''[[Dark Souls]]'' (2011), which influenced the combat system, particularly its gameplay loop and strategic decision-making,<ref>{{cite web|title=God of War's New Combat System Explained|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D_JNQKlA57k|website=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[PlayStation]]|date=March 19, 2018|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418073325/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D_JNQKlA57k|archive-date=April 18, 2018}}</ref> as well as the approach to storytelling.<ref>{{cite magazine|title="It Has to Be Personal" Says 'God of War' Creative Director Cory Barlog|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/glixel/features/it-has-to-be-personal-says-god-of-war-creative-director-cory-barlog-w488948|last=Davison|first=John|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=June 20, 2017|access-date=May 1, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501161717/https://www.rollingstone.com/glixel/features/it-has-to-be-personal-says-god-of-war-creative-director-cory-barlog-w488948|archive-date=May 1, 2018}}</ref> In addition, designers Anthony DiMento and Luis Sanchez revealed how ''God of War''{{'}}s level design and exploration were influenced by ''[[Bloodborne]]'' (2015). They wanted to "just have the world breathe a little bit" and expand upon player discovery by including "micro-loops where you're unlocking paths, unlocking shortcuts" that gave purpose.<ref>{{cite magazine|title='God of War' Level Design Inspired by 'Bloodborne'|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/glixel/news/god-of-war-level-design-inspired-by-bloodborne-w518527|date=March 29, 2018|last=Fogel|first=Stefanie|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=May 15, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515184739/https://www.rollingstone.com/glixel/news/god-of-war-level-design-inspired-by-bloodborne-w518527|archive-date=May 15, 2018}}</ref> DiMento said that a team dedicated to the exploration was formed. One challenge was creating quests in a world that did not have [[non-playable characters]] outside of the core narrative. DiMento said, "I set out to create a quest giver that was light-weight, but also flexible enough to be used in multiple locations, while providing a varied suite of quest activities". This resulted in the "wayward spirits" (ghosts with ties to the world) found throughout the game. Having the spirits tell their stories "made [the world] feel more alive". The developers ended up with a four-tiered system for side quests: the top-tier quests were from the characters Brok and Sindri, the next level from wayward spirits, then treasure maps and artifacts, and the bottom tier were milestones, such as killing all of [[Odin's ravens]]. Brok and Sindri's quests were made into [[Dungeon crawl|dungeons]] while the others were used for exploration. The developers also had to find the reasons that would motivate Kratos to undertake these quests. For Brok and Sindri, it was to obtain more powerful gear, but for the wayward spirits, it was because of Atreus's naiveté and kind-hearted nature, as well as opportunities for Kratos to teach him life lessons.<ref name="exploration">{{cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/12/05/how-santa-monica-studios-nailed-exploration-in-god-of-war/|title=How Santa Monica Studio Nailed Exploration in God of War|date=December 5, 2018|last=DiMento|first=Anthony|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|access-date=December 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181217154733/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/12/05/how-santa-monica-studios-nailed-exploration-in-god-of-war/|archive-date=December 17, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Unlike the previous games, Santa Monica did not make a demo for public release. Barlog said that doing so would have delayed development by a couple of months.<ref name="Nopublicdemo">{{cite web|url=http://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2016/10/13/god-of-war-demo-ps4-pro/|title=God of War Designed for Standard PS4, Won't Have a Demo|last=Treese|first=Tyler|date=October 13, 2016|publisher=[[CraveOnline]]|work=[[PlayStation LifeStyle]]|access-date=February 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413201034/http://www.playstationlifestyle.net/2016/10/13/god-of-war-demo-ps4-pro/|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also confirmed ''God of War'' was built for the standard PlayStation 4<ref name="Nopublicdemo"/> but would "benefit from the power" of the [[PlayStation 4 Pro]], which was released a few months after ''God of War'' was announced.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=corybarlog|author=Cory Barlog|author-link=Cory Barlog|number=787432956474327040|date=October 15, 2016|title=oh we will benefit from the power of the Pro, for sure. You just dont need a pro to get the experience we intend.|archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/6yemtcH9u?url=https://twitter.com/corybarlog/status/787432956474327040|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Players with a Pro have the option to favor resolution or performance. Favoring resolution runs the game in 4K with [[checkerboard rendering]] at a target frame rate of 30 [[frames per second]] (fps), while the performance option runs the game at [[1080p]] and targets 60fps.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/4/12/17227946/god-of-war-ps4-pro-60fps-4k-1080p|title=God of War's 4K resolution mode isn't the best way to play|date=April 12, 2018|last=Sarkar|first=Samit|work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|publisher=[[Vox Media]]|access-date=November 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114155518/https://www.polygon.com/2018/4/12/17227946/god-of-war-ps4-pro-60fps-4k-1080p|archive-date=November 14, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> In late December 2016, Barlog confirmed ''God of War'' was playable from start to finish,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-ps4-game-reaches-very-exciting-mile/1100-6446477/|title=New God of War PS4 Game Reaches "Very Exciting Milestone"|date=December 22, 2016|last=Makuch|first=Eddie|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|access-date=December 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413201913/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-ps4-game-reaches-very-exciting-mile/1100-6446477/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> and later said its story would take 25–35 hours to complete (significantly more than the previous four main installments, which each took an average of 10 hours to complete).<ref name="longgame">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-will-take-25-35-hours-to-complete/1100-6455531/|title=God Of War PS4 Will Take 25–35 Hours To Complete|date=December 8, 2017|last=Newhouse|first=Alex|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=December 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413194153/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-will-take-25-35-hours-to-complete/1100-6455531/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref>

A trailer was also released that showed that the mythological character Mímir would have a role.<ref name="releasedate">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2018/01/23/god-of-war-will-release-in-april.aspx|title=God Of War Releases On April 20|last=Juba|first=Joe|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|publisher=[[GameStop]]|date=January 23, 2018|access-date=January 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413202026/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2018/01/23/god-of-war-will-release-in-april.aspx|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> ''God of War'' [[went gold]] on March 22.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-has-gone-gold/1100-6457615/|title=God Of War PS4 Has Gone Gold|date=March 22, 2018|last=Knezevic|first=Kevin|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=March 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413202316/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-has-now-gone-gold/1100-6457615/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref>

===Characterization===
[[File:Christopher Judge 2014.jpg|thumb|right|upright|alt= A photograph of actor Christopher Judge; he did the voice and cinematic motion capture for Kratos in the game. | [[Christopher Judge]] does the voice and cinematic [[motion capture]] for [[Kratos (God of War)|Kratos]], replacing  [[Terrence C. Carson|T.C. Carson]], who had voiced Kratos since the [[God of War (2005 video game)|original 2005 game]] and also provided the [[motion capture]] in 2013's ''[[God of War: Ascension|Ascension]]''.]]
During early development, there was talk of having a different protagonist. Some of the team said that Kratos was "annoying" and felt Kratos's story had run its course. Barlog said it took a lot of convincing to keep Kratos.<ref name="annoying">{{cite web|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-06-26-cory-barlog-discusses-almost-cutting-kratos-from-god-of-war-2018|title=Cory Barlog discusses almost cutting Kratos from God of War 2018|date=June 26, 2019|last=Evans-Thirlwell|first=Edwin|work=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|access-date=July 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629043919/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2019-06-26-cory-barlog-discusses-almost-cutting-kratos-from-god-of-war-2018|archive-date=June 29, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> Referencing the [[Nintendo]] character [[Mario]] and the [[Mario (franchise)|''Mario'' games]], Barlog said that like Mario, "Kratos is intrinsically tied" to the ''God of War'' series.<ref name="TakeKratosSeriously"/> In regard to the new changes, Barlog said that:

{{Blockquote|I knew I didn't want to simply reboot the franchise, starting over with a retelling of the [[origin story]]. I wanted to reimagine the gameplay, give players a fresh perspective and a new tactile experience while delving deeper into the emotional journey of [[Kratos (God of War)|Kratos]] to explore the compelling drama that unfolds when an immortal demigod makes a decision to change.<ref name="Kratoschange"/>}}

Barlog explained that Kratos had to change his cycle of violence and learn to control his rage. He said Kratos had made many bad decisions, which led to the destruction of [[Mount Olympus|Olympus]]. He wanted to know what would happen if Kratos made a good decision. The birth of Barlog's own son influenced the idea of Kratos's character change.<ref name="Kratoschange">{{cite web|url=http://blog.us.playstation.com/2016/06/13/first-look-santa-monica-studios-new-god-of-war-on-ps4/|title=First Look: Santa Monica Studio's New God of War on PS4|date=June 13, 2016|last=Barlog|first=Cory|author-link=Cory Barlog|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|access-date=June 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413202516/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2016/06/13/first-look-santa-monica-studios-new-god-of-war-on-ps4/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> The canceled live-action [[Star Wars#Live-action series|''Star Wars'' television series]] developed by [[George Lucas]] during the 2000s was also an influence; back on his days working at [[LucasArts]], Barlog had been allowed to visit [[Skywalker Ranch]] and read some scripts written by writers of ''[[The Shield]]'' and ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]'' planned for the show, particularly starring [[Emperor Palpatine]] in an emotional and sympathetic [[origin story]] that depicted his fall into villainy after being wronged by a heartless woman.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2016/06/20/god-of-war-director-cory-balrog-says-that-sonys-violent-series-is-growing-up-with-the-industry/|title=God of War director Cory Barlog says that Sony's violent series is growing up with the industry|date=June 20, 2016|last=Minotti|first=Mike|publisher=[[VentureBeat]]|access-date=June 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413202418/https://venturebeat.com/2016/06/20/god-of-war-director-cory-balrog-says-that-sonys-violent-series-is-growing-up-with-the-industry/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> The bond between Kratos and his son is at the heart of the game. Barlog said, "This game is about Kratos teaching his son how to be a god, and his son teaching Kratos how to be human again".<ref name="MadeMeCare"/> Referencing the [[Marvel Comics]] character [[Hulk]], Barlog said that in regards to Kratos, "We've already told the story of The Hulk. We want to tell the story of [Bruce] Banner now".<ref name="MadeMeCare"/> One of their goals was to make Kratos "a more nuanced and interesting character".<ref name="GIp44">{{harvnb|ref=GIcoverstory|Juba|2018|p=44}}</ref> In changing the narrative focus, Studstill said, "I think we inherently knew the franchise needed to evolve in that emotional beat and be something meatier for the older generation of gamers."<ref name="GIp44"/>

Christopher Judge, best known as [[Teal'c]] from ''[[Stargate SG-1]]'', replaced [[Terrence C. Carson]] as the voice of Kratos; Carson had voiced Kratos since the original ''God of War'' game. Carson said "Sony went in a new direction".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-does-not-feature-original-kratos-vo/1100-6440925/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0a|title=New God of War Does Not Feature Original Kratos Voice Actor|date=June 15, 2016|last=Paget|first=Mat|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[GameSpot]]|access-date=June 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413202827/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-god-of-war-does-not-feature-original-kratos-vo/1100-6440925/?ftag=GSS-05-10aaa0a|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Carson later said that he understood the reason and that Judge's casting made sense for what Sony was wanting to do. He also said that losing acting jobs is part of the business, but he did feel a lack of respect as he was not contacted by anyone at Sony.<ref>{{cite video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ohW0A_qEPjI|title=TC Carson on Voicing 'Kratos" in 'God of War' 1-3, Why He Got Replaced (Part 6)|date=December 31, 2020|author=[[DJ Vlad]]|work=VladTV|publisher=[[YouTube]]|time=3:15–5:16|access-date=January 4, 2021|archive-date=February 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202160858/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ohW0A_qEPjI|url-status=live}}</ref>

In explaining the actor change, Barlog said that the way the previous games were made, they were able to have someone else do the [[motion capture]] instead of the voice actor. Although Carson had done the motion capture for Kratos in ''Ascension'', Barlog said the actor change was made because of the type of camera work they wanted to do. For the new camera work, they needed someone who was closer to Kratos's size to do the motion capture along with a child. Carson was unsuitable for this because he was much shorter than Kratos, who is over {{Convert|6|ft|cm|abbr=out}} tall: "Offsetting [Carson's height] for the size of a child, it turned out it was going to be almost impossible to try and actually shoot them and go in and redo the animations".<ref name="NewVO">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/god-war-4-ps4-game-hinges-bond-2-new-actors-1043888|title='God of War' Hinges on the Bond of Its 2 New Actors|date=September 29, 2017|last=Shanley|first=Patrick|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=February 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413191831/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/god-war-4-ps4-game-hinges-bond-2-new-actors-1043888|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Judge was chosen because he was {{convert|6|ft|3|in|cm|abbr=out}} and had the build of a professional football player. He was also chosen because of the chemistry with his then-10-year-old co-star Sunny Suljic, whose opinion was also sought in making the decision; out of all the auditions, he liked Judge the most. The two bonded well, and Judge described his time with Suljic as time he had missed with his own children. In stepping into the role of Kratos, Judge took it as an opportunity to add something new to the character. He researched the character and Carson's performance but decided not to imitate it. Since Santa Monica was going in a new direction, he decided to start fresh. Judge was thrown off when he first read the script, saying it "was a real script," and not just "a way to get into battles," which is why he decided to take the role.<ref name="NewVO"/> He said, "it was really this great story of this relationship and this crazy mythology".<ref name="NewVO"/> While Judge did all of Kratos's motion capture for the cinematic scenes, stuntman Eric Jacobus did Kratos's combat motion capture; Jacobus was found by ''God of War''{{'}}s animators on [[YouTube]]. Instead of going directly to Santa Monica to audition, he recorded and submitted an audition tape and was hired immediately.<ref>{{cite AV media|people=Jacobus, Eric|date=March 28, 2018|title=God of War – How to Fight Like Kratos, PS4|medium=[[YouTube]]|language=en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rKuc73DSscs|access-date=May 11, 2018|publisher=[[PlayStation]], [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180505014815/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rKuc73DSscs&app=desktop|archive-date=May 5, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Former [[WWE]] wrestler [[Shad Gaspard]] also performed some of the motion capture for Kratos.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=Shadbeast|author=[[Shad Gaspard]]|number=989923203366600704|date=April 27, 2018|title=I did know 😜 now so does the rest of the world 🤣 such an honor and a privilege to be part of this game and play this character that I've always loved. Thank you @rafagrassetti and #GodOfWar team at @santamonicastudio|access-date=January 1, 2021}}</ref>

During E3 2016, ''[[GameSpot]]'' mistakenly reported that Kratos's son's name was Charlie, which Barlog laughingly denied.<ref>{{cite AV media|people=Shuman, Sid; [[Cory Barlog|Barlog, Cory]]; [[Judge, Christopher]]|date=June 14, 2016|title=God of War – E3 2016 LiveCast|medium=[[YouTube]]|language=en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ar59w0yrA_E|access-date=June 15, 2016|publisher=[[PlayStation.Blog]], [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|time=13:35|quote='''Shuman:''' Does the son have a name by the way? '''Barlog:''' Uh, GameSpot says it's Charlie. '''Shuman:''' Charlie? '''Barlog:''' Charlie! [laughs] I don't know where that came from. '''Shuman:''' That's fun. [laughs] '''Barlog:''' Charlie, right? [looks at Judge] Did you leak that? '''Judge:''' I did. [laughs]|ref=LiveCast|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413191912/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ar59w0yrA_E|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In reference to this, the giant turtle above Freya's house was named Chaurli.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thegamer.com/god-of-war-atreus-trivia/|title=God of War: 10 Things You Didn't Know About Atreus|date=February 21, 2021|last=Roxl|first=Rhett|work=TheGamer|access-date=November 15, 2022|archive-date=November 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116003659/https://www.thegamer.com/god-of-war-atreus-trivia/|url-status=live}}</ref> In January 2017, after a fan downloaded the ''God of War'' [[overture]] and saw the track's details that read, "An introduction to Kratos and Atreus", Barlog confirmed on [[Twitter]] that Atreus was in fact the son's name.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/01/13/god-of-war-kratos-sons-name-revealed|title=God of War: Kratos' Son's Name Revealed|date=January 13, 2017|last=Osborn|first=Alex|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|work=[[IGN]]|access-date=January 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413203249/http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/01/13/god-of-war-kratos-sons-name-revealed|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> Barlog said Atreus was unaware that Kratos was a [[demigod]] and did not know about his past.<ref name="single-player-only"/> They did not reveal details of Atreus's mother before the release because she was a critical part of the story.<ref name="WCCF"/> Barlog said that during gameplay, Atreus would be "like magic, an additional combat resource, and [the player is] training him and teaching him".<ref name="TakeKratosSeriously"/> The developers said Atreus would not be a burden during gameplay.<ref name="axeorigin"/> The team experimented with several different approaches for Atreus to ensure he was an empowering presence. Barlog said he did not want the game to be an [[escort mission]] wherein the [[Artificial intelligence in video games|artificial intelligence]] causes a problem for the player. Their goal was for Atreus to enhance Kratos's capabilities without becoming a liability. This resulted in the developers having Atreus act freely unless the player uses a button to issue specific commands to him.<ref name="GIp42"/> Atreus was also designed to call out enemy locations during combat. Since the camera is closer to Kratos, some enemies might be difficult for the player to see. Lead gameplay designer Jason McDonald said that it took a lot of iterations with the enemies and Atreus to make it all work together.<ref name="developingaxe"/>

Early in development, it was suggested that Atreus be cut, or his role significantly reduced because of the many developmental challenges and their costs. Barlog said the game could have worked without Atreus, but it would have been completely different, likening it to the 2013 film ''[[All Is Lost]]''. Barlog said that with just Kratos, it would have been "one character who talks to himself occasionally, but generally, it will be very silent and everyone will talk in [[old Norse]], so that you won't understand anything anybody's saying".<ref name="NoAtreus"/> After hearing Barlog's case, Sony gave him the freedom to incorporate Atreus. Lead level designer Rob Davis also noted that Atreus allowed for "significant gameplay and storytelling opportunities that might not otherwise [have been] possible".<ref name="NoAtreus">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-almost-didnt-have-one-of-its-best-m/1100-6458294/|title=God Of War PS4 Almost Didn't Have One Of Its Best, Most Important Characters|date=April 17, 2018|last=Makuch|first=Eddie|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=May 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422051552/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-almost-didnt-have-one-of-its-best-m/1100-6458294/|archive-date=April 22, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> After ''God of War'' was revealed at E3 2016, it drew comparisons to [[Naughty Dog]]'s ''[[The Last of Us (video game)|The Last of Us]]'' (2013), a game that also featured a father-child type story and gameplay. Barlog felt it was "fantastic" to be compared to that game and found it odd that some people considered the similarities a negative thing. He said: "I think we're all inspired by each other."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gamingbolt.com/to-be-compared-to-the-last-of-us-is-fantastic-says-god-of-war-director|title=To Be Compared to The Last of Us is Fantastic, Says God of War Director|date=May 25, 2018|author=Pramath|work=GamingBolt.com|access-date=December 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181217154616/https://gamingbolt.com/to-be-compared-to-the-last-of-us-is-fantastic-says-god-of-war-director|archive-date=December 17, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> He used ''The Last of Us'' to demonstrate to the development team how an in-game companion could work without escort missions.<ref name="annoying"/>
