''God of War (PlayStation Soundtrack)'' was released on April 20, 2018, by [[Sony Classical Records]]. It was composed by [[Bear McCreary]], who is best known for his work on television shows like ''[[Battlestar Galactica (2004 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' and ''[[The Walking Dead (TV series)|The Walking Dead]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2016/06/14/e3-2016-new-god-of-war-announced/|title=E3 2016: New God of War Announced|date=June 14, 2016|last=Davis|first=Justin|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|work=[[IGN]]|access-date=June 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413204155/http://www.ign.com/articles/2016/06/14/e3-2016-new-god-of-war-announced/|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref> McCreary was called into Santa Monica Studio in November 2014 to meet with music producers Peter Scaturro and Keith Leary to discuss "a secret project"; McCreary had previously collaborated with Scaturro and Leary on 2011's ''[[SOCOM 4: U.S. Navy SEALs]]''. Ideas of folk music, mythology, Nordic ethnic instruments, vocal writing, and classical thematic development were discussed; McCreary correctly guessed that the discussions were about a new ''God of War''. McCreary met with Barlog early on to discuss his narrative vision. After meeting with him, McCreary felt the franchise was in good hands because ''God of War II'', which Barlog also directed, was his favorite installment.<ref name="McCrearyblog"/>

During the initial discussions, McCreary realized he needed to compose new music and not reuse music from the series.<ref name="Spotify"/> He said that although he loved those games, he "would not describe them as emotionally dynamic".<ref name="Revolver"/> Based on his memory of the earlier games' music, however, he was inspired by their sounds, such as "deep choirs, pounding drums, and shrieking brass", and reinvented them for the Nordic setting.<ref name="Spotify"/> To ensure the music represented the setting, McCreary spent months researching and listening to Viking folk music,<ref name="Revolver">{{cite web|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/culture/god-war-how-viking-folk-music-inspired-audacious-new-games-soundtrack|title='God of War': How Viking Folk Music Inspired "Audacious" New Game's Soundtrack|date=April 24, 2018|last=Winkie|first=Luke|work=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|publisher=Project M Group LLC|access-date=November 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112043503/https://www.revolvermag.com/culture/god-war-how-viking-folk-music-inspired-audacious-new-games-soundtrack|archive-date=January 12, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> which resulted in him using "exotic instrumentation and languages from various Northern European folk traditions".<ref name="Spotify"/> He also wanted the score to be huge and varied, "full of peaks and valleys, tiny incantations and gigantic set pieces".<ref name="Revolver"/> The main Kratos theme in particular features low orchestral instruments, an [[Icelandic music|Icelandic]] choir, deep male vocals, powerful female vocals (in particular [[Faroe Islanders|Faroese]] singer [[Eivør Pálsdóttir]]), folk percussion, and Nordic stringed instruments, like the [[nyckelharpa]] and [[hurdy gurdy]].<ref name="McCrearyblog"/> The track "Witch of the Woods" uses a renaissance and baroque instrument called a [[viola da gamba]], which is an ancestor of the modern [[cello]]. The Stranger's theme, found in the track "Deliverance", uses a [[Hardanger fiddle]].<ref name="Themes"/>

The first theme composed was "Memories of Mother". McCreary said the theme itself was not originally for Atreus's mother Faye, but for Kratos himself. His initial drafts were different variations of this melancholy tune. After ''God of War'' had gone into full production, McCreary and the development team realized it was "too sad and lyrical to represent Kratos". McCreary stepped away from this theme and focused on writing a new one, or what he called the Kratos Theme, which he felt was more representative of the character: "masculine, relentless, and badass".<ref name="Spotify">{{cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/04/13/how-bear-mccreary-composed-god-of-wars-soundtrack-out-today-on-spotify/|title=How Bear McCreary Composed God of War's Soundtrack, Out Today on Spotify|date=April 13, 2018|author=McCreary, Bear|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|access-date=November 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112043503/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/04/13/how-bear-mccreary-composed-god-of-wars-soundtrack-out-today-on-spotify/|archive-date=January 12, 2019|url-status=live|author-link=Bear McCreary}}</ref> He spent several months working with Barlog, Scaturro, Leary, Sony music director Chuck Doud, and the rest of the development team to make this new theme. McCreary described it as "arguably one of my most structurally satisfying and catchy melodies".<ref name="McCrearyblog">{{cite web |url=https://bearmccreary.com/god-of-war-at-e3/ |title=God of War at E3 |date=June 27, 2016 |last=McCreary |first=Bear |author-link=Bear McCreary |access-date=September 1, 2023 |website=BearMcCreary.com |archive-date=August 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240827154553/https://bearmccreary.com/god-of-war-at-e3/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After further scoring, McCreary realized that Faye would require a theme, and his original one was "exactly [what] I needed". This melody was woven throughout several scenes and is featured as prominently as Kratos's theme.<ref name="Spotify"/> The three-note Kratos theme is most obviously heard in the title track, "God of War".<ref name="Themes">{{cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/05/08/the-themes-of-god-of-war/|title=The Themes of God of War|date=May 8, 2018|author=McCreary, Bear|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|access-date=November 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181005021835/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/05/08/the-themes-of-god-of-war/|archive-date=October 5, 2018|url-status=live|author-link=Bear McCreary}}</ref>

When it was decided that ''God of War'' would be revealed at E3 2016, Sony wanted McCreary to perform his original score with a live orchestra at the press conference. McCreary opened the show with the new main theme before the unveiling of ''God of War'' and performed the gameplay demo's music live during the presentation.<ref name="McCrearyblog"/> On January 13, 2017, a live recording from E3 2016 of ''God of War''{{'}}s overture was released for a limited time free of charge. Barlog released the overture as a thank you to fans for ''God of War''{{'}}s E3 2016 trailer reaching fifteen million views on YouTube.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2017/01/download_god_of_wars_live_e3_2016_overture_for_free|title=Download God of War's Live E3 2016 Overture for Free|date=January 13, 2017|last=Barker|first=Sammy|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|work=[[Push Square]]|access-date=January 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413192640/http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2017/01/download_god_of_wars_live_e3_2016_overture_for_free|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Release==
''God of War'' was released worldwide on April 20, 2018, for the PlayStation 4.<ref name="releasedate"/> In addition to the standard base game, there were three special editions: the Stone Mason Edition, the Collector's Edition, and the Digital Deluxe Edition. The Stone Mason Edition was only available in the United States and Canada and came with several physical items, including: the base game in a SteelBook case, a {{convert|9|in|adj=on}} statue of Kratos and Atreus created by Gentle Giant, {{convert|2|in|adj=on}} carvings of the Huldra Brothers, a horse, and a troll, an exclusive [[lithograph]], a cloth map, a [[stonemason]]'s ring, and a keychain of Mímir's head that talks. There was a variety of [[downloadable content]] (DLC), including an exclusive shield skin, as well as an armor set and another shield skin for Kratos, a PlayStation 4 dynamic theme, a digital artbook, and ''[[God of War (comics)|God of War]]'' #0 by [[Dark Horse Comics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4s-collectors-edition-revealed-comes-/1100-6456168/|title=God Of War PS4's Collector's Edition Revealed, Comes With An Epic Statue Of Kratos And More|date=January 18, 2018|last=Faller|first=Patrick|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=January 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119120050/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4s-collectors-edition-revealed-comes-/1100-6456168/|archive-date=January 19, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Collector's Edition came with many of the same items, minus the ring, the keychain, the carvings of the horse and troll, and the exclusive shield skin. The Digital Deluxe Edition came with all the digital content, minus the exclusive shield skin. U.S. and Canadian customers also received a Kratos and Atreus [[Award pin|pin]] for pre-ordering the Digital Deluxe Edition. Pre-orders at select retailers received three skins for Kratos's shield. Pre-orders from [[GameStop]] or [[EB Games]] also received the "Luck of Ages XP Talisman", granting increased XP and Hacksilver gains and increased ability to trigger perks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/01/23/god-of-war-out-april-20-on-ps4/|title=God of War Out April 20 on PS4|date=January 23, 2018|author=Barlog, Cory|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|access-date=January 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413203647/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/01/23/god-of-war-out-april-20-on-ps4/|archive-date=April 13, 2018|author-link=Cory Barlog}}</ref>

In addition to the special editions, a Limited Edition PlayStation 4 Pro bundle was available the same day as the game. The bundle included the standard base game, a PlayStation 4 Pro console decorated with the runes on Kratos's axe, and a similarly themed [[DualShock 4]] controller with the ''God of War'' logo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-pro-bundle-unveiled-by-sony/1100-6457190/|title=God of War PS4 Pro Bundle Unveiled by Sony|date=April 13, 2018|last=Pereira|first=Chris|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=April 13, 2018|archive-date=February 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220207121355/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-pro-bundle-unveiled-by-sony/1100-6457190/|url-status=live}}</ref> Additionally, an official [[Tabletop game|tabletop]] [[card game]] titled ''God of War: The Card Game'' was released by [[CMON Limited]] on October 25, 2019. Created by Alexandru Olteanu and Fel Barros, players take on the role of the [[Norns]], the [[Fates]] of Norse mythology, as they try to prevent Ragnarök with different combinations of characters and events from the game, providing many variations to completing the card game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cmon.com/news/cmon-announces-god-of-war-the-card-game|title=CMON Announces God of War: The Card Game|date=April 16, 2019|work=[[CMON Limited]]|access-date=January 8, 2023|archive-date=January 8, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230108122138/https://cmon.com/news/cmon-announces-god-of-war-the-card-game|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cmon.com/news/god-of-war-the-card-game-developer-q-a|title=God of War: The Card Game Developer Q&A|date=May 9, 2019|work=[[CMON Limited]]|access-date=January 8, 2023|archive-date=January 8, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230108122139/https://cmon.com/news/god-of-war-the-card-game-developer-q-a|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tabletopgamingnews.com/God-of-War--The-Card-Game-Now-Available|title=God of War: The Card Game Now Available|date=October 28, 2019|author=Polar_Bear|work=Tabletop Gaming News|publisher=BV Software|access-date=January 8, 2023|archive-date=January 8, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230108122138/https://www.tabletopgamingnews.com/God-of-War--The-Card-Game-Now-Available|url-status=live}}</ref>

Prior to launch, Barlog confirmed that ''God of War'' would not have [[microtransaction]]s, a feature that had become prominent with other games and criticized.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-wont-have-microtransactions-says-direct/1100-6457222/|title=God Of War Won't Have Microtransactions, Says Director|date=March 8, 2018|last=Knezevic|first=Kevin|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=March 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318065527/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-wont-have-microtransactions-says-direct/1100-6457222/|archive-date=March 18, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also confirmed that it would not have post-release DLC, like an [[expansion pack]]. He said he had pitched an idea for DLC, "but it was too ambitious". His idea was similar in scope to that of ''[[The Last of Us: Left Behind]]'' (2014) and ''[[Uncharted: The Lost Legacy]]'' (2017), large standalone expansions for ''The Last of Us'' (2013) and ''[[Uncharted 4: A Thief's End]]'' (2016), respectively. He said it would have been too big to be DLC, warranting its own standalone release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-dlc-idea-scrapped-for-being-too-ambitio/1100-6464263|title=God Of War DLC Idea Scrapped For Being "Too Ambitious"|date=January 9, 2019|last=Makuch|first=Eddie|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=June 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190623213101/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-dlc-idea-scrapped-for-being-too-ambitio/1100-6464263/|archive-date=June 23, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

Post-launch, Santa Monica supported ''God of War'' with [[Patch (computing)#Video games|patch updates]] to address [[software bug]]s. As well, the developers added new features along with these free updates. A Photo Mode was released as part of update patch 1.20 on May 9, 2018. It allows players to take customized in-game screenshots. Players can adjust the field of view, depth of view, filters, borders, the visibility of characters, and the ability to change the facial expressions of Kratos and Atreus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/05/09/photo-mode-comes-to-god-of-war-today/|title=Photo Mode Comes to God of War Today|date=May 9, 2018|last=Shroff|first=Jeet|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|access-date=May 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512044655/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/05/09/photo-mode-comes-to-god-of-war-today/|archive-date=May 12, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> A [[New Game Plus]] mode was released as part of update patch 1.30 on August 20, 2018. To access the mode, players must have completed the game at any difficulty level. The mode itself can be played at any difficulty, but enemies are at a higher level with new maneuvers. All obtained items carry over to New Game Plus, and there are new resources to further upgrade gear, which also have new rarity levels. The option to skip cutscenes was also added.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/06/11/first-details-new-game-mode-in-god-of-war/|title=First Details: New Game+ Mode in God of War|date=June 11, 2018|last=Kaufman|first=Aaron|work=[[PlayStation.Blog]]|publisher=[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]]|access-date=June 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612190911/https://blog.us.playstation.com/2018/06/11/first-details-new-game-mode-in-god-of-war/|url-status=live|archive-date=June 12, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/08/god-of-war-new-game-release-date-announced-details-revealed|title=God of War New Game+ Release Date Announced, Details Revealed|date=August 8, 2018|last=Gilyadov|first=Alex|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|access-date=August 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809132103/http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/08/08/god-of-war-new-game-release-date-announced-details-revealed|archive-date=August 9, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2018/08/god_of_war_patch_1_30_adds_new_game_plus_out_now_on_ps4|title=God of War Patch 1.30 Adds New Game +, Out Now on PS4|date=August 20, 2018|last=Ramsey|first=Robert|work=[[Push Square]]|publisher=[[Gamer Network]]|access-date=August 21, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821094212/http://www.pushsquare.com/news/2018/08/god_of_war_patch_1_30_adds_new_game_plus_out_now_on_ps4|url-status=live|archive-date=August 21, 2018}}</ref> In November 2020, the [[PlayStation 5]] (PS5) launched and is [[backwards compatible]] with PlayStation 4 games; these games see a performance boost when playing on the PS5. To further enhance the playing experience of ''God of War'' on the PS5, Santa Monica released an update on February 2, 2021, allowing it to be played at 60 fps with checkerboard-rendered [[4K resolution]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.techradar.com/news/god-of-war-ps5-update-makes-one-of-the-best-ps4-games-even-better|title=God of War PS5 update makes one of the best PS4 games even better|date=February 2, 2021|last=Vjestica|first=Adam|work=[[TechRadar]]|access-date=February 4, 2021|archive-date=February 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203064950/https://www.techradar.com/news/god-of-war-ps5-update-makes-one-of-the-best-ps4-games-even-better|url-status=live}}</ref>

As part of Sony's larger efforts to port their first-party exclusive games to [[Windows]], Santa Monica Studio announced in October 2021 that ''God of War'' would be released for Windows on January 14, 2022. The port, handled by Jetpack Interactive with supervision by Santa Monica, includes additional graphic options support for Windows, including [[Nvidia]]'s [[Deep Learning Super Sampling]] (DLSS) technology and ultra-widescreen support. This in turn marks the first main entry in the series to release on a non-PlayStation platform.<ref name="psblog windows">{{cite web | url = https://blog.playstation.com/2021/10/20/god-of-war-2018-is-coming-to-pc/ | title = God of War (2018) is coming to PC | first = Grace | last = Orlady | date = October 20, 2021 | access-date = October 20, 2021 | work = [[PlayStation Blog]] | archive-date = October 20, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211020161747/https://blog.playstation.com/2021/10/20/god-of-war-2018-is-coming-to-pc/ | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/god-of-war-pc-version-developer/|title=God of War for PC Isn't Being Developed by Santa Monica Studio|date=October 25, 2021|last=Moore|first=Logan|work=[[Comic Book Resources]]|publisher=Valnet Inc.|access-date=October 26, 2021|archive-date=October 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026101319/https://comicbook.com/gaming/amp/news/god-of-war-pc-version-developer/|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Santa Monica's Matt DeWald, they had considered what options they could use to port their games to Windows, particularly as they used a non-standard [[game engine]], and worked closely with Jetpack to determine the scope and technical issues associated with the port.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.theverge.com/22883541/god-of-war-pc-port-interview | title = HOW GOD OF WAR'S IMPRESSIVE PC PORT CAME TO LIFE | first = Sam | last = Byford | date = January 14, 2022 | access-date = January 14, 2022 | work = [[The Verge]] | archive-date = January 14, 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220114143857/https://www.theverge.com/22883541/god-of-war-pc-port-interview | url-status = live }}</ref>

===''God of War: A Call from the Wilds''===
'''''God of War: A Call from the Wilds''''' was a [[text-based game]] that was only playable through [[Facebook Messenger]].{{efn|The game is no longer available.}} To help further promote ''God of War'', Sony partnered with [[Meta Platforms|Facebook]] to develop the [[play-by-web]] game, which released on February 1, 2018. Completing the game unlocked downloadable concept art. The short story followed Atreus on his first adventure in the Norse wilds. After archery training and learning runes with his mother, Atreus ventures into the wilderness after telepathically hearing the voice of a dying deer; he finds it covered in blood and stays with it during its final moments. A couple of draugr appear and Atreus attempts to fight them but is injured. He is saved by his father, Kratos, who was out hunting. The two then battle a revenant before returning home.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/02/01/god-of-war-facebook-text-adventure-explores-atreus-past|title=God of War Facebook Text Adventure Explores Atreus' Past|date=February 1, 2018|last=Gilyadov|first=Alex|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|access-date=February 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413203931/http://www.ign.com/articles/2018/02/01/god-of-war-facebook-text-adventure-explores-atreus-past|archive-date=April 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/heres-how-to-play-god-of-war-early-in-official-text-adventure-form/|title=Here's how to play God of War early (in official text adventure form)|date=February 2, 2018|last=Sheridan|first=Connor|work=[[GamesRadar+]]|publisher=[[Future plc]]|access-date=February 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413192310/https://www.gamesradar.com/heres-how-to-play-god-of-war-early-in-official-text-adventure-form/|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2018/02/01/glimpse-into-atreus-past-in-god-of-war-text-adventure.aspx|title=Glimpse Into Atreus' Past In God Of War Text Adventure|date=February 1, 2018|last=Thurmond|first=Joey|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|publisher=[[GameStop]]|access-date=February 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413192352/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2018/02/01/glimpse-into-atreus-past-in-god-of-war-text-adventure.aspx|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

===''Raising Kratos''===
'''''Raising Kratos''''' is a YouTube documentary of Santa Monica Studio's five-year development process, showing the "herculean effort" that went into reviving the franchise. Unlike the previous ''two God of War'' novels, it closely follows the source material with a few notable exceptions. The game never revealed how or why Kratos was in ancient Norway, or how much time had passed since the ending of ''God of War III'', but the novel gives some indication. Kratos chose to leave ancient Greece to hide his identity and change who he was.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|p=34}}</ref> At some point after leaving Greece, he battles some wolves and is saved by a cloaked female figure, presumably Faye.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|p=22}}</ref> Later, during their journey, Kratos, Atreus, and Mímir see a mural with the wolves [[Sköll]] and [[Hati Hróðvitnisson|Hati]]. This causes Kratos to have a flashback to the initial battle and makes him wonder if they dragged him to this new land and if so, why.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|p=250}}</ref> There was also some [[retconning]]; at the end of ''God of War III'', Kratos had the Blades of Exile, but this novel says he had the Blades of Chaos after killing Zeus. It is also mentioned that he tried several times to get rid of the blades, but by fate they kept returning to him. (For example, he threw them off a cliff, but they washed up on shore near him.) Sometime after ending up in Norway, he decided to hide them under his house and never use them again. This moment was said to have occurred 50 years before the start of the current story. When Kratos does recover the Blades of Chaos, he hears [[Pandora]]'s speech about hope from ''God of War III''.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|pp=224–225}}</ref>

In the game, Kratos sees one last image on the mural in Jötunheim. It seemingly shows Atreus holding Kratos's dead body, but in the novel, this mural is partially broken and does not show the corpse that Atreus is holding.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|p=340}}</ref> Brok and Sindri also reveal why they made the Leviathan Axe for Faye; she had come to them as the last Guardian of Jötnar and needed a weapon to protect her people. The Huldra Brothers crafted the Leviathan Axe for her to be Mjölnir's equal. Mímir also mentioned that Faye, or rather Laufey the Just, thwarted many of the Æsir's plans, including freeing slaves, and Thor could never find her.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|p=347}}</ref> Kratos's Guardian Shield is never mentioned, and Modi does not ambush the three, resulting in Atreus falling ill; Atreus instead falls ill shortly after their first encounter when Kratos kills Magni.<ref>{{harvnb|ref=GoW2018novel|Barlog|2018|loc=chpt. 34–35}}</ref>

of War'' received particular praise for its art direction, graphics, combat system, music, story, use of Norse mythology, characters, and cinematic feeling. Many reviewers felt it had successfully revitalized the series without losing the core identity of its predecessors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-reviews-roundup-updated/1100-6458186/|title=God Of War PS4 Reviews Roundup|work=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180416012619/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/god-of-war-ps4-reviews-roundup-updated/1100-6458186/|archive-date=April 16, 2018|url-status=live|access-date=April 15, 2018}}</ref>

The story was well praised. Nick Plessas of ''[[Electronic Gaming Monthly]]'' (''EGM'') said the story's most memorable moments were the interactions between Kratos and Atreus. He also noted, "there is often some comic relief to be found when Kratos's curtness and Atreus's charming naivety collide."<ref name="EGMreview"/> He felt the presence of Atreus showed a side to Kratos not seen before, and that Kratos had evolved emotionally: "The rage and pain of his past is in constant conflict with his desire to spare his son from it, which comes across in even the most subtle actions and words, demonstrating the effort he is putting in." Plessas said Atreus's character was similarly complex. He commented it is easy for child characters "to succumb to a number of annoying child archetypes," but Atreus is more like a young man who is doing his best in an adult world.<ref name="EGMreview"/> ''[[Game Informer]]''{{'}}s Joe Juba similarly praised the story, particularly the relationship between Kratos and Atreus: "The interactions of Kratos and Atreus range from adversarial to compassionate, and these exchanges have ample room to breathe and draw players in." Juba said that Kratos conveys more character than in any previous game.<ref name="GIreview"/> Peter Brown of ''GameSpot'' felt that although Kratos and Atreus were enjoyable, it was Mímir who stole the show. He also said that regardless of which character the player meets, the cast of ''God of War'' is "strong, convincing, and oddly enchanting."<ref name="GSpotreview"/> Writing for ''[[Game Revolution]]'', Jason Faulkner praised Santa Monica for creating a sequel that new players would be able to understand without having played any of the previous games, while at the same time providing story references to those past games that returning fans would appreciate. Speaking of the relationship between Kratos and Atreus, Faulkner wrote that, "Watching the two grow throughout their journey is incredibly rewarding," equating it to that of [[Ellie (The Last of Us)|Ellie]] and [[Joel (The Last of Us)|Joel]] from ''The Last of Us'' or [[Lee Everett|Lee]] and [[Clementine (The Walking Dead)|Clementine]] from [[Telltale Games]]'s ''[[The Walking Dead (video game series)|The Walking Dead]]''.<ref name="GameRevreview"/>

Plessas said that unlike previous games, which often relied on the player to use many combos in a sequential fashion, ''God of War'' is "more about individual moves strung together in response to the assortment of enemies being fought." Although that difference may be small, he said that the independent attacks of the axe "feature benefits and drawbacks players will need to understand and master to be as effective as possible." Furthermore, although the axe is "conceptually simple", it is "mechanically fascinating". It "succeeds as both a versatile means of dismembering foes and as a key element in puzzle solving." He felt the axe and all of its features was "distinctly rewarding to use" and that it had more versatility than all of the weapons in many other games.<ref name="EGMreview"/> Juba said the Leviathan Axe is "a well-balanced and entertaining tool of destruction." He liked how it "emphasizes a more calculated style of combat; instead of zoomed-out, combo-driven encounters, Leviathan makes you a tactician." He also enjoyed how the combat system gradually unfolded; although seemingly restrictive at first, he noted players will be rapidly alternating between weapons and skills.<ref name="GIreview"/> While some reviewers greatly enjoyed the ability to call the Leviathan Axe back to Kratos's hand,<ref name="GIreview"/><ref name="IGNreview"/> Chris Carter of ''[[Destructoid]]'' felt it got old after a while.<ref name="Destructreview"/> Atreus's implementation was praised; Plessas said Atreus is "surprisingly useful" and that he "lands in the perfect spot on the spectrum between independence and reliance."<ref name="EGMreview"/> Faulkner noted that, "The interplay between Kratos ax, fists, and shield, and Atreus's bow makes for an impressive fighting system."<ref name="GameRevreview"/> Despite its different approach to combat, ''[[GamesRadar+]]''{{'}}s Leon Hurley felt ''God of War''  was "every bit as brutally unflinching as previous games".<ref name="GRadarreview"/>

Writing for ''[[Polygon (magazine)|Polygon]]'', Chris Plante praised the camerawork as a technical marvel, noting the seamless shift from cinematic back to the gameplay.<ref name="Polygonreview"/> Juba said the decision to shift the camera closer to Kratos "[proved] immensely rewarding during big moments by giving [the player] an intimate view."<ref name="GIreview"/> Faulkner, however, claimed "it can be difficult to control the camera and keep a bead on the enemies you're fighting."<ref name="GameRevreview"/> In his review for ''[[IGN]]'', Jonathon Dornbush felt the intimacy of the camera makes all the emotions "more real and impactful."<ref name="IGNreview"/> Faulkner said the visuals were amazing, "and with 4K and [[High dynamic range|HDR]] this game goes a step beyond what even games like ''[[Horizon Zero Dawn]]'' showed us was possible on this platform."<ref name="GameRevreview"/> Brown noted that "''God of War'' is a technical and artistic showcase. It is without a doubt one of the best-looking console games ever released."<ref name="GSpotreview"/> Dan Ryckert of ''[[Giant Bomb]]'' claimed that games like ''Uncharted: The Lost Legacy'' and ''Horizon Zero Dawn'' "made great cases for a PS4 Pro and a 4K television, but ''God of War''{{'}}s visuals are a bigger selling point than anything I've seen on Sony's platform to date."<ref name="GBreview"/>

Plessas felt that the boss fights "do not hit quite the same frequency as they did in the past few games". However, the few boss fights "do the series proud".<ref name="EGMreview"/> As to the vast world of ''God of War'', Faulkner said that, "The great thing about the exploration in ''God of War'' is that you can participate in it as little or as much as you want." He said an excellent design decision is that during main plot points, the game keeps the player on task, while in between, the player can explore, allowing ''God of War'' "to have the best of both worlds".<ref name="GameRevreview"/> Plessas noted that although the puzzles require thought, they were not "hair-pullingly" difficult as some were in previous games.<ref name="EGMreview"/> Juba also found that the puzzles were not too challenging, saying they were fun.<ref name="GIreview"/>

Plessas felt that the RPG elements made ''God of War'' unique. He said players could "specialize Kratos to meet the specific task at hand, or develop a build that best suits a preferred playstyle". Although this did not make the game easier, he felt it did make it more manageable.<ref name="EGMreview"/> Juba noted that although this type of upgrading "may be less exciting" compared to previous games where Kratos just learns new moves, it still "provides a powerful incentive to explore."<ref name="GIreview"/> Ryckert was disappointed by this type of customization. He felt the presentation was "half-baked" and that some materials were confusing as there was little explanation given for their use. He did, however, say it was "cool" to see new armor on Kratos.<ref name="GBreview"/>

In terms of flaws, Plessas said that "''God of War'' is so good that its most egregious failing is not letting fans play more of it", as New Game Plus was not an option at the time of the review.<ref name="EGMreview"/> Juba said that "''God of War''{{'}}s momentum rarely falters, and when it does, the inconvenience is brief." One example he gave was the map, saying that although players have freedom to explore, it can be difficult to track Kratos's position. He also felt the fast-travel system was "weirdly cumbersome" and that it opens up too late.<ref name="GIreview"/> Although he enjoyed these features, Faulkner noted some players may dislike that ''God of War'' has a lack of player agency, and players have to explore the majority of the game on foot or by boat since the fast-travel feature is unlocked late.<ref name="GameRevreview"/> Brown felt that if anything in ''God of War'' was a letdown, it was the final fight against Baldur: "He's great from a narrative standpoint, unraveling in a manner that changes your perspective, but it's the fight itself that leaves you wanting. There are plenty of big boss battles and tests of skill throughout the course of the game, yet this fight doesn't reach the same heights, and feels like it was played a little safe."<ref name="GSpotreview"/> Hurley said his only criticism was that, "You can occasionally find yourself unsure if you're doing something wrong, or don't have the right equipment yet."<ref name="GRadarreview"/>

== Sequel ==
{{main|God of War Ragnarök}}
Following ''God of War''{{'}}s announcement in mid-2016, Barlog confirmed that it would not be Kratos's last game.<ref name="single-player-only"/> He also said that after the Norse era, future games could see the series tackling [[Egyptian mythology|Egyptian]] or [[Maya mythology]],<ref name="GIp45"/> and although the 2018 installment focused on Norse mythology, it alluded to other mythologies co-existing in the world.<ref>{{cite AV media|people=[[Cory Barlog|Barlog, Cory]]; Studstill, Shannon|date=January 9, 2018|title=Norse and Beyond: Expanding God of War's Mythology|medium=[[YouTube]]|language=en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CzW2sBmR5CQ&t=15s|access-date=February 1, 2018|publisher=[[Game Informer]], [[GameStop]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413190910/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CzW2sBmR5CQ&t=15s|archive-date=April 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barlog also said he liked the idea of having different directors for each game, as had happened with the Greek era, and that although he might not direct another ''God of War'', he would still be at Santa Monica to work on future games.<ref name="GIquestions"/>

A sequel, ''[[God of War Ragnarök]]'', was announced at the PlayStation 5 Showcase event in September 2020 and was originally scheduled to be released in 2021.<ref>{{cite ==Television series==
{{main|God of War (American TV series)}}
In March 2022, it was reported that a [[live action]] television series was said to be in development at [[Amazon Prime Video]] by [[Mark Fergus]], [[Hawk Ostby]], and [[Rafe Judkins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=March 7, 2022 |title='God of War' TV Series Adaptation Eyed By Prime Video |url=https://deadline.com/2022/03/god-of-war-tv-series-prime-video-playstation-amazon-studios-1234959867/ |access-date=March 7, 2022 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]] |language=en-US |archive-date=May 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220526080655/https://deadline.com/2022/03/god-of-war-tv-series-prime-video-playstation-amazon-studios-1234959867/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During an investor briefing that May, [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]] president Jim Ryan confirmed that a ''God of War'' television series was in development for Prime Video.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/sony-horizon-series-netflix-god-of-war-amazon-gran-turismo-tv|title=Sony Announces Horizon Series for Netflix, God of War Series for Amazon, and a Gran Turismo Show|date=May 26, 2022|last=Dinsdale|first=Ryan|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]|access-date=May 26, 2022|archive-date=May 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220526143217/https://www.ign.com/articles/sony-horizon-series-netflix-god-of-war-amazon-gran-turismo-tv|url-status=live}}</ref> The series was officially ordered in December 2022 and is being produced by [[Sony Pictures Television]] and [[Amazon Studios]] in association with [[PlayStation Productions]], and it will premiere on Prime Video in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. Executive producers include Barlog, PlayStation Productions's Asad Qizilbash and Carter Swan, Santa Monica Studio's Yumi Yang, and [[Vertigo Entertainment]]'s [[Roy Lee]], with Santa Monica Studio's Jeff Ketcham serving as a co-executive producer. The series will adapt the Norse era, beginning with the events of the 2018 installment.<ref name="Prime-production">{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2022/12/god-of-war-adaptation-playstation-video-game-series-order-prime-video-1235198842/|title='God Of War' Adaptation Of PlayStation Video Game Gets Prime Video Series Order|date=December 14, 2022|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]]|access-date=December 14, 2022|archive-date=December 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221214180431/https://deadline.com/2022/12/god-of-war-adaptation-playstation-video-game-series-order-prime-video-1235198842/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Amazon Studios's Head of Television, Vernon Sanders, assured that the series would stay true to the game. Implying that there could be multiple seasons, Sanders said that the "emotional core" of the first season, and series as a whole, would be the father-and-son story.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/god-of-war-series-source-material-vernon-sanders-comments/|title='God of War' Series Will Be "True to Source Material" Says Amazon Studios' Vernon Sanders [Exclusive]|date=December 19, 2022|last=Villei|first=Matt|work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|publisher=Valnet, Inc.|access-date=December 21, 2022|archive-date=December 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221220235247/https://collider.com/god-of-war-series-source-material-vernon-sanders-comments/|url-status=live}}</ref> Qizilbash stated that they would apply the same amount of care that they did with [[The Last of Us (TV series)|the television adaptation]] of ''The Last of Us'', stating that they would be telling the whole story of the game, as without the time constraints of a film, they have multiple episodes to be able to tell the story.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/god-of-war-horizon-tv-show-the-last-of-us-similar-playstation-productions/|title=God of War and Horizon TV Producer Claims Shows Will Be Similar to The Last of Us|date=April 21, 2023|last=Onder|first=Cade|work=[[ComicBook.com]]|publisher=[[Paramount Global]]|access-date=May 23, 2023|archive-date=April 22, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422091841/https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/god-of-war-horizon-tv-show-the-last-of-us-similar-playstation-productions/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

The series was originally being written by Fergus and Ostby, with Judkins serving as showrunner, who were all also going to be executive producers.<ref name="Prime-production"/> By January 2024, writing was underway.<ref name="WritingBegins">{{Cite web |last=Barnhardt |first=Adam |date=January 8, 2024 |title=Sony Shows Gravity Rush Movie, Updates on God of War and Horizon Shows |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/sony-shows-gravity-rush-movie-updates-on-god-of-war-and-horizon-shows |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240109045325/https://www.ign.com/articles/sony-shows-gravity-rush-movie-updates-on-god-of-war-and-horizon-shows |archive-date=January 9, 2024 |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[Ziff Davis]]}}</ref> In October, however, it was reported that while multiple scripts for the first season had been completed and although both Sony and Prime gave praise, Fergus, Ostby, and Judkins left the project as the studios wanted to start over and go in a different direction.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/god-of-war-sony-executive-producers-depart-new-writers-joining-1236118075/|title='God Of War': Sony And Amazon Starting Over On Series After Departure Of EPs Rafe Judkins, Hawk Ostby & Mark Fergus|date=October 17, 2024|last=Rice|first=Lynette|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]]|access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> Prolific creator and showrunner [[Ronald D.
